summary: Willamette NF summit lookout: 1920s shake cabin, L-4 cab in 1931, a lookout on duty in 1930, later abandoned and gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1931) per FFLOS and firelookout.com; Oregon Lookouts describes a 14 x 14 gable-roof lookout house instead
facts.status_note: FFLOS says the lookout was abandoned and is gone; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: lookout and smoke chaser who spent summers on the summit (1930 newspaper item)

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Willamette National Forest

events.note: Anthony Nuttman, lookout and smoke chaser, spent summers on the summit (1930 Daily Capital Journal item as quoted by Oregon Lookouts)
Shake cabin replaced by an L-4 cab per FFLOS and firelookout.com; Oregon Lookouts instead dates a 14 x 14 gable-roof lookout house to about 1931
Date registered November 18, 2019 per FFLOS (US 1827, OR 550)

evidence.supports: site is in the Willamette National Forest, about 12 miles south of Mount Jefferson
1930 newspaper item put the summit at 6,000 feet
evidence.quote: Red Butte has an elevation of 6,000 feet.

evidence.supports: shake cabin built in the 1920s, replaced by an L-4 cab in 1931
evidence.quote: In the 1920's a shake cabin was constructed on the site which was replaced by a L-4 cab in 1931.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com gives shake cabin in the 1920s and L-4 cab in 1931
Oregon Lookouts describes a 14 x 14 gable-roof lookout house dated about 1931
evidence.quote: c.1931: A 14 x 14 gable roof lookout house constructed.

evidence.supports: October 1930 newspaper item described Anthony Nuttman as a lookout and smoke chaser who summered on top of Red Butte
evidence.quote: Anthony Nuttman, lookout and smoke chaser, in the employ of the forest service, who spends his summers on the top of Red Butte

evidence.supports: register says the lookout was later abandoned and is gone
evidence.quote: The lookout was later abandoned and is gone.

evidence.supports: Oregon Lookouts marks the site as removed

corrections.why: The FFLOS Built field reads 1920's and firelookout.com reads 1920s; neither gives a single year, so 1920 claims more precision than the sources do

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 5,843 ft (1,781 m), which matches the record. A 1930 newspaper item quoted by Oregon Lookouts says 6,000 feet. The story reports both figures and does not pick one.

FFLOS and firelookout.com both say a shake cabin was replaced by an L-4 cab in 1931. Oregon Lookouts describes a 14 x 14 gable-roof lookout house built about 1931. The story reports both descriptions and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Three pages only. They agree on the 1920s shake cabin, the 1931 rebuild and the abandonment, but Oregon Lookouts describes the 1931 building as a 14 x 14 gable-roof house and gives 6,000 feet, not the L-4 cab and 5,843 feet the other two give. The county is recorded as Linn, but firelookout.com says Lane County; not checked against a county map, so the record is unchanged. Oregon Lookouts marks the site removed with no date. No source describes the site today. Photos: FFLOS credits a 1920s-1931 photo to the Howard Verschoor collection, but no image URL was captured, so none is listed. A 1933 panorama is mentioned on Oregon Lookouts (dated 11 September 1933); a FFLOS caption dates one 9-30-1933, seen only in a search snippet and not checked on the page.
